Building a microkernel in Rust

My final project for an operating-systems class, exploring IPC, capabilities, scheduling, and resource domains.

I built a Rust microkernel as my final project for an operating-systems class. It explores inter-process communication, capability-based access control, scheduling, and resource domains.

The repository includes the implementation, tests, and a documented bare-metal QEMU boot path. I used it to learn about operating-system boundaries, not to build a production operating system.

Most of my other work runs on top of an OS. This project was a chance to work on the abstractions beneath those programs instead.
